subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should managed Browser upload keep paths-only arming as a supported default, or should agent/tool flows prefer or require atomic upload-with-trigger behavior for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both paths-only arming and same-request trigger upload are supported today, and changing the default can improve reliability while also changing the Browser API expectations for existing callers.

options.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
options.body: Keep paths-only arming valid, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing same-request trigger path when a chooser trigger is known.

options.title: Retire delayed trigger arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref/inputRef/element for managed upload flows and provide migration guidance for callers that depended on delayed chooser arming.

options.title: Document current workaround only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations, accepting that dynamic-page flakes can remain.

recommendation.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming valid, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing same-request trigger path when a chooser trigger is known.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant upload/control API history is tied to Peter Steinberger's Browser control and bundled-plugin ownership work.
